1: function T = ashuganj_transformers()
2: %ASHUGANJ_TRANSFORMERS  Transformer database - Ashuganj 450 MW CCPP SOUTH.
3: %
4: %   T = ASHUGANJ_TRANSFORMERS() returns a struct array with one element per
5: %   power transformer, populated for the Specialized Power Systems
6: %   "Three-Phase Transformer (Two Windings)" block in PER-UNIT units.
7: %
8: %   Three transformers exist in the South plant:
9: %       GSUT 10BAT10   230/22   kV   355/460/515 MVA  ONAN/ODAN/ODAF  YNd1
10: %       UAT  10BBT10    22/6.9  kV    19/25     MVA  ONAN/ONAF       Dyn11
11: %       GAT  10BBT20   230/6.9/3.32 kV  19/25   MVA  ONAN/ONAF       YNyn0+d11
12: %
13: %   The GAT was ABSENT from the prior CYME PSAF model (defect D6).  Its
14: %   presence closes a loop: 230 kV -> GSUT -> 22 kV -> UAT -> 6.6 kV -> GAT ->
15: %   230 kV.  Approved answer Q4c keeps BOTH states (GAT in / GAT out) as
16: %   separate load-flow cases so the loop effect can be reported.
17: %
18: %   -------- Impedance convention -------------------------------------
19: %   Nameplates give the magnitude Z (%) and the resistance R (%) at a stated
20: %   MVA base.  The reactance is therefore DERIVED, not read:
21: %       X = sqrt(Z^2 - R^2)                                   [pu]
22: %   and is split equally between the two windings, R1 = R2 = R/2 and
23: %   L1 = L2 = X/2, because the nameplate gives only the total leakage
24: %   impedance and no winding-by-winding split exists in the source set.
25: %   The equal split is a REPRESENTATION CHOICE, not a claimed measurement;
26: %   in a two-winding load flow only the series total R + jX affects the
27: %   result, so the split has no numerical consequence at all.
28: %
29: %   -------- Magnetising branch ---------------------------------------
30: %   BOTH magnetising elements are now DERIVED from documented data.
31: %
32: %   Rm from the documented no-load LOSS:
33: %       Rm(pu) = S_rated / P_no-load
34: %   Lm from the documented no-load CURRENT, by removing the loss
35: %   component that Rm already carries:
36: %       (1/Lm)^2 = I0^2 - (1/Rm)^2        =>  Lm = 1/sqrt(I0^2 - (1/Rm)^2)
37: %   with I0 the datasheet excitation current at 100 % rated voltage, in pu
38: %   of rated current on the same MVA base as Rm and Z.
39: %
40: %   HISTORY - this replaces an earlier treatment that set Lm = 1e6 pu
41: %   (numerically open) on the stated ground that "no-load current is absent
42: %   from every nameplate in the set".  That claim was true of the rating
43: %   PLATES and false of the DATA SHEETS: the GSUT sheet publishes 0.13 %
44: %   and the UAT/GAT sheet publishes ~0.3 % and 0.3 %.  The assumption was
45: %   written before those two documents had been read.  It is retired, not
46: %   tweaked; matlab/data/assumptions/transformer_magnetising_inductance.m
47: %   is kept as a SUPERSEDED record of the error rather than deleted.
48: %
49: %   Effect of the correction, stated as two DIFFERENT quantities so they
50: %   are not confused:
51: %     - magnetising reactive draw now represented, which the open-circuit
52: %       treatment omitted entirely:  0.650 + 0.074 + 0.071 = 0.795 MVAr
53: %       (S_rating/Lm per unit, at 1.0 pu terminal voltage);
54: %     - the resulting shift in the GENERATOR's reactive output is smaller
55: %       than that, because the machine is a PV bus and the 230 kV swing
56: %       supplies part of the extra demand.  It is MEASURED, not asserted,
57: %       by matlab/tests/test_magnetising_sensitivity.m.  The retired
58: %       assumption's published worst case of +3.4406 MVAr on that same
59: %       generator quantity was taken at a 1 % magnetising current, i.e.
60: %       7.7x the GSUT's documented 0.13 %, so it bounded the error safely
61: %       but very loosely.
62: %
63: %   The documented load loss independently CORROBORATES the documented R:
64: %       GSUT  1095 kW / 515 MVA = 0.2126 %  vs nameplate 0.21 %  (+1.2 %)
65: %       UAT    110 kW /  25 MVA = 0.4400 %  vs nameplate 0.40 %  (+10 %)
66: %       GAT    116 kW /  25 MVA = 0.4640 %  vs nameplate 0.50 %  (-7.2 %)
67: %   The nameplate R is used; the load-loss figure is retained as the
68: %   cross-check and the spread is reported.
69: %
70: %   See also ASHUGANJ_MASTER_DATA, CONVERT_TO_SYSTEM_BASE.
71:

165: peak = continuous+v('load_trip_kW')+v('load_close_kW')+v('load_emergency_additional_kW');

168: consistent = consistent && peak<v('charger_rated_power_kW') && ...
169:     1000*peak<=v('charger_max_current_A')*v('dc_cutoff_voltage_V') && ...
170:     1000*peak/v('dc_cutoff_voltage_V')<v('dc_max_discharge_A');

178: name = parts{1};

194: switch old.source_status

196:             'VERIFIED_ENGINEERING_DOCUMENT','PRIMARY_VERIFIED'}

1: function Ld = ashuganj_loads()
2: %ASHUGANJ_LOADS  Load database - Ashuganj 450 MW CCPP SOUTH.
3: %
4: %   Ld = ASHUGANJ_LOADS() returns a struct array of the auxiliary loads.
5: %
6: %   TOTAL AUXILIARY LOAD: 14 MW at 0.85 power factor.
7: %   ------------------------------------------------------------------
8: %   A WARNING about this number, carried from the audit: 14 MW happens to be
9: %   numerically equal to the UAT no-load loss expressed in kW (14 kW) and to
10: %   3.60 % of the 389.30 MW rated output.  Those are COINCIDENCES.  The 14 MW
11: %   is the documented plant auxiliary load; the 14 kW is the UAT iron loss.
12: %   They are unrelated quantities that share two digits, and the resemblance
13: %   was checked and dismissed during the audit rather than being allowed to
14: %   propagate as a transcription error.
15: %
16: %   ALLOCATION (approved answer Q6B): the load is DISTRIBUTED across three
17: %   6.6 kV nodes in the ratio 9050 : 2500 : 2500, which comes from the
18: %   documented motor ratings (kW) of the main auxiliary group and the two
19: %   water-intake / large-motor groups.  The RATIO is grounded in documented
20: %   motor ratings; the ALLOCATION OF THE 14 MW TOTAL ACROSS THAT RATIO IS AN
21: %   APPROVED ASSUMPTION, because no per-node metered demand exists.  The user
22: %   required this to be labelled an assumption and it is:
23: %       matlab/data/assumptions/aux_load_allocation_split.m
24: %
25: %   Because the 6.6 kV feeder impedances are MISSING (see ASHUGANJ_LINES),
26: %   the three nodes are joined with zero impedance.  The split therefore
27: %   segregates the load for REPORTING and for the later protection study; it
28: %   does not produce feeder voltage drop.  Total P and Q drawn from the UAT
29: %   are identical to the single-bus case - that is a correctness property,
30: %   not a defect, and it is stated in the report.
31: %
32: %   POWER FACTOR: 0.85 lagging is applied to every node.  A per-node power
33: %   factor is NOT documented; using one figure for all three nodes avoids
34: %   inventing three.
35: %
36: %   LOAD MODEL: constant PQ.  A load flow that used constant impedance would
37: %   silently reduce the auxiliary demand whenever the solved voltage sagged,
38: %   which would flatter the result.  Constant PQ holds the documented demand.
39: %
40: %   See also ASHUGANJ_MASTER_DATA, ASHUGANJ_BUSES.
41: 
42: % ---- Documented totals -------------------------------------------------
43: P_total_MW  = 14.0;
44: P_Status    = 'VERIFIED_PROJECT_DATA';
45: P_Source    = 'Project data set - plant auxiliary load 14 MW';
46: pf          = 0.85;
47: pf_Status   = 'VERIFIED_PROJECT_DATA';
48: pf_Source   = 'Project data set - auxiliary load power factor 0.85 lagging';
49: 
50: Q_total_MVAr = P_total_MW*tan(acos(pf));
51: 
52: % ---- Allocation ratio from documented motor ratings (kW) ---------------
53: alloc_kW    = [9050, 2500, 2500];
54: alloc_nodes = {'B6_6', 'B6_6_WI1', 'B6_6_WI2'};
55: alloc_label = {'MV BUS aux group', 'Water intake / motor group 1', ...
56:                'Water intake / motor group 2'};
57: share       = alloc_kW/sum(alloc_kW);
58: 
59: k = 0; Ld = struct([]);
60: for i = 1:numel(alloc_nodes)
61:     k=k+1;
62:     Ld(k).Name             = ['LOAD_' alloc_nodes{i}];
63:     Ld(k).Label            = alloc_label{i};

%
%   The block is oriented 'down' so that the 230 kV winding is on top and the

function Z = build_gsut_system(mdl, D)
%BUILD_GSUT_SYSTEM  Generator step-up transformer zone, Ashuganj South.
%
%   Z = BUILD_GSUT_SYSTEM(MDL, D) adds GSUT 10BAT10 to model MDL. The block's
%   position comes from SPS_GEOM: it stands in the GSUT column and spans the
%   230 kV BUS 1 tier down to the 22 kV GEN BUS tier, because its two winding
%   terminals ARE those two bus nodes. SPS_GEOM asserts that span, so the
%   transformer cannot drift off either busbar without the build stopping.
%
%   GSUT 10BAT10 : 230/22 kV, ONAN/ODAN/ODAF 355/460/515 MVA, YNd1,
%                  OLTC 25 taps on HV, principal tap 9 = 230000 V,
%                  Z = 16 % and R = 0.21 % at 515 MVA,
%                  no-load loss 159 kW, load loss 523/874/1095 kW.
%
%   The block is oriented 'down' so that the 230 kV winding is on top and the
%   22 kV winding at the bottom, which is how a plant one-line diagram is
%   drawn. Winding 1 stays the HV winding, exactly as the nameplate lists it,
%   so the YNd1 vector group maps directly onto the block.
%
%   TAP (approved answer Q8a): principal tap 9, which is 253000 - 8*2875 =
%   230000 V exactly, so the modelled ratio is precisely nominal. Taps are
%   NOT optimised to improve the solved voltage profile.
%
%   Note on the impedance base: the SPS block takes per-unit values on ITS
%   OWN NominalPower, which is how the nameplate quotes them, so nothing is
%   converted here. Converting to the 100 MVA reporting base at this point
%   would be a double conversion; that base is used only for reporting.

B  = sps_blocks();
t  = D.tx(strcmp({D.tx.Name},'GSUT'));
g  = sps_geom();
cx = g.col.gsut;

Z.tx = sps_wire('add', mdl, B.tx2, t.Label, ...
                g.box(cx, g.tier.bus1, g.tx), 'down');
apply_transformer_params(Z.tx, t);
% Filled in the 230 kV tint, outlined in the 230 kV ink: the GSUT straddles two
% levels, and it is the HV side that decides which switchyard it belongs to.
set_param(Z.tx, 'BackgroundColor', g.clr.fill230, ...
                'ForegroundColor', g.clr.v230);

Z.node_HV = sps_wire('port', Z.tx, 'L');   % 230 kV, on top,    on BUS 1
Z.node_LV = sps_wire('port', Z.tx, 'R');   % 22 kV, at bottom,  on the 22 kV bus

% ---- Labels ----------------------------------------------------------
% Tag, ratio, vector group, rating, impedance - and stop. The derived detail
% (R and X separately, X/R, Rm, Lm, the tap arithmetic) moves to the parameter
% table at the foot of the diagram, where it can be read as a table instead of
% competing with the one-line for space. A plant drawing captions a transformer
% in three lines and so does this.
%
% Annotation Position is only honoured at its left and top edge - Simulink
% refits the right and bottom to the text - so these are anchors and the space
% to the right of them is left deliberately clear.
sps_wire('note', mdl, 'GSUT  10BAT10', ...
    [cx+58, g.tier.bus1+14, cx+238, g.tier.bus1+36], 11, 'bold', g.clr.v230);
sps_wire('note', mdl, sprintf(['230/22 kV  YNd1  Z = %.1f %%\n' ...
    '355/460/515 MVA  ONAN/ODAN/ODAF\ntap %d/%d = %g V (principal)'], ...
    t.Z_pct, t.Tap_used, t.Tap_positions, t.Tap_V_used_V), ...
    [cx+58, g.tier.bus1+40, cx+298, g.tier.bus1+94], 9, 'normal');

Z.report = pack_report(t);
end

% =====================================================================
function apply_transformer_params(blk, t)
%APPLY_TRANSFORMER_PARAMS  Populate one SPS two-winding transformer block.
%   Shared by the GSUT and auxiliary zone builders so that the parameter
%   mapping exists in exactly one place.
set_param(blk, ...
    'UNITS',              'pu', ...
    'NominalPower',       sprintf('[ %.10g , %.10g ]', t.S_rating_MVA*1e6, t.f_Hz), ...
    'Winding1',           sprintf('[ %.10g , %.12g , %.12g ]', t.V_HV_V, t.R1_pu, t.L1_pu), ...
    'Winding2',           sprintf('[ %.10g , %.12g , %.12g ]', t.V_LV_V, t.R2_pu, t.L2_pu), ...
    'Winding1Connection', t.Conn_HV, ...
    'Winding2Connection', t.Conn_LV, ...
    'CoreType',           t.Model_coretype, ...
    'SetSaturation',      t.Model_saturation, ...
    'Rm',                 sprintf('%.10g', t.Rm_pu), ...
    'Lm',                 sprintf('%.10g', t.Lm_pu), ...
    'L0',                 sprintf('%.10g', t.L0_pu));
sps_wire('setopt', blk, 'Measurements', 'None');
end

% =====================================================================
function r = pack_report(t)
r = struct('Name', t.Name, 'V_HV_V', t.V_HV_V, 'V_LV_V', t.V_LV_V, ...
           'S_rating_MVA', t.S_rating_MVA, 'S_MVA', t.S_MVA, ...
           'Z_pct', t.Z_pct, 'R_pct', t.R_pct, 'X_pct', t.X_pct, ...
           'XR', t.XR_ratio, 'Rm_pu', t.Rm_pu, 'Lm_pu', t.Lm_pu, ...
           'Conn_HV', t.Conn_HV, 'Conn_LV', t.Conn_LV, ...
           'VectorGroup', t.VectorGroup, 'Tap', t.Tap_used);
end
